To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Soft tissue tumors of head and neck are a heterogeneous collection of neoplasmas that arise from adipose, fibrous, or muscular tissues.

(i) Imaging of benign and malignant neck masses is usually with CT and MRI; (ii) Imaging is needed to assess location and extent of tumor prior to biopsy; (iii) Imaging features may help distinguish benign and malignant soft-tissue tumors from other neck tumors; (iv) The behavior of these tumors varies from benign to highly aggressive.

1) imaging is important in the evaluation and management of neck soft tissue tumors; 2) CT and MR are complementary and provide important information about tumor size, location, and extent; 3) the imaging features are often characteristic and can be helpful in distinguishing benign from malignant tumors, and in separating one type of tumor from another; and 4) imaging is important for treatment planning, and for assessing tumor recurrence and metastasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the imaging of benign and malignant neoplasms of the soft tissue of the neck.
the development of a new method for the development of a soft tissue tumors of head and neck.

the study of soft-tissue tumours in the neck, with the aim of establishing a diagnostic algorithm for these tumours based on the imaging findings, which will help the radiologist to suggest the correct diagnosis.

soft tissue tumors of neck are rare.

imaging of soft tissue tumors of neck is very important in order to assess the location, extent and behavior of the tumor.

the imaging of benign and malignant tumors of the neck is a very important part of the diagnostic work-up.

the imaging features of soft tissue tumors of neck are highly variable, and the diagnosis of such lesions can be difficult, especially when they occur in unusual locations.
